findings.title: lexChar moves `lx->pos` by hand and never advances line/col, so every diagnostic after a character literal on the same line points at the wrong column
findings.why: The file's own contract (lexer.c:122-124) says "Do not advance the cursor any other way. `pos` and `line`/`col` have to move together or every later diagnostic points at the wrong place." lexChar finds the closing quote by raw index arithmetic and then assigns `lx->pos = close + 1` without touching `lx->col` (lxAdvance is never called on the simple `'a'` path). All later tokens on that line therefore carry the column of the opening quote. The error caret is visibly misplaced: `var x = 'a' + )` reports column 16 (under `+`) for a `)` that is at column 18, while the identical line written as `97 + )` reports 18.
findings.trigger: Any lexical or syntax error on a source line that contains a character literal earlier on the same line (the drift is the literal's byte length).

findings.title: Float literals that overflow or underflow are accepted silently (`1e999` becomes infinity), while the integer path diagnoses ERANGE
findings.why: The integer branch clears errno, converts, and reports ERANGE; the float branch calls strtod and ignores both the return value and errno. `1e999` therefore lexes to +inf and codegen emits `__builtin_inf()` with no diagnostic, and `1e-999` silently becomes 0.0 -- a mistyped exponent turns into a value the source never spelled, which is exactly the failure mode the integer path is written to prevent ("integer literal exceeds the supported signed 64-bit range").
findings.trigger: A float literal whose value is outside the double range, e.g. `1e999`, `1e-999`, `1e400`.

coverage_notes: Read src/lexer.c (581 lines) and src/lexer.h (79 lines) line by line (all of it, no sampling). Covered: token kinds and Token layout; lexIsPunct + inList/isKeyword/isBuiltinType; character classes (ASCII only); Lexer state and lxPeek/lxAdvance/lxPushAt/lxLast; lexNumber (decimal, 0x hex with overflow pre-check, fraction and exponent, strtoll/strtod); lexIdent (keyword/type classification, the reserved `__` prefix rule); lexString (escape validation via lexEscape, verbatim copy of escapes, newline and EOF handling); lexEscape (all escapes, \xHH, unknown escape); lexChar (closing-quote scan, `\\` handling, single-byte enforcement, escape decode); lexPunct (longest-match-by-table-order, <<,>> deliberately absent); lexAll (whitespace, CRLF, newline collapsing and trailing newline, line/block comments, error returns); tokenKindName and tokenDescribe. Cross-checked and found NOT to be defects: the newline-collapsing and always-append-trailing-newline rules hold (verified through the parser's use of TK_EOF); PUNCTS is ordered so that `->`, `==`, `<=`, `..`/`...`, `::`, `=>`, `??` and the compound assignments all win over their prefixes; lexChar's quote scan handles `'\\''`, `'\\\\'` and `'\x41'` correctly (traced); a source ending in `"\\` makes lexEscape advance past the end once, but both callers keep a NUL one byte past the end (readWholeFile allocates n+1 and writes buf[got]=0, src/base.c:599-611; the prelude is a NUL-terminated literal), so it is not an out-of-bounds read today -- noted as fragile, not reported; lexIdent reports the reserved `__` prefix but lexAll does not return on it (lexer.c:533 has no hasError check, unlike the number/string/char branches), which only means the rest of the file is scanned after the error -- harmless because ctxError keeps the first error (src/base.c) and every caller skips parsing when ctx->hasError is set (main.c:415/436/443, modules.c:1828), so it is recorded here rather than as a finding. The consequence of the discarded string length (lexer.h:27-29 exists so a NUL inside a literal survives) is reported as a parser-level finding in parser-3.json, because the loss happens when the parser copies only t->text into EX_STR.
